title: Controlled Dynamics Attractor Transformer
claim: Plain gradient descent gets stuck in spurious local minima on a rugged landscape; adding inhibition and structural priors reaches the global optimum.
layout: 1 central contour landscape with 3 corner graph insets, arrows linking trajectory to outputs
description: A large 3D-style contour map of an energy landscape fills the center, with several hills and basins drawn as black topographic lines. A pale yellow start point at the top connects by a blue arrow to an Input graph at upper left. It shows several red anomalous nodes among blue nodes. From the start, a black dashed path with blue state dots descends into a shallow trap marked by a red dot. Blue arrows link that trap to a lower-left graph labeled Best Response of Baseline Methods. That graph still has two red nodes, so it is wrong. A purple CDAT trajectory winds along the valley, with small red self-inhibition arrows and gray aggregation arrows. It ends at a green dot in the global minimum. A blue arrow links the green dot to a lower-right graph labeled CDAT output (Correct). That graph has all nodes blue.
caption: CDAT dynamics. The figure shows the representation trajectories on the energy landscape. While the negative-gradient baseline (black dashed) gets trapped in a spurious local minimum, CDAT (purple) reaches the global minimum via self-inhibition (red) that repels the state from shallow traps and topology-aware aggregation (gray) that steers it with structural priors.
abstract: Transformer architectures have dramatically advanced representation learning and inference in deep models through self-attention mechanisms. In parallel,associative memory (AM) frameworks map representations onto energy landscapes, offering interpretable retrieval mechanisms. However, their continuous-time inference dynamics lack the biological plausibility of classical Continuous Attractor Neural Networks (CANNs). To bridge this gap, we propose Controlled Dynamics Attractor Transformer (CDAT), which couples a mixture von Mises-Fisher (Mo-vMF) attention energy with a Hopfield refinement energy, while augmenting energy descent with a CANN-inspired excitation-inhibition modulation. CDAT instantiates a topology-constrained dynamical system whose couplings encode relational structure among tokens, thereby linking attractor-style dynamics to modern energy-based attention. We further provide a constructive dissipation analysis to formally establish their controlled inference dynamics. Benefiting from these robust and structured dynamics, CDAT achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks in graph anomaly detection and graph classification.
